security_spec.violation_condition: ChiselIOPMP/src/main/scala/IopmpChecker.scala:565-616 — MDLCK, MDCFGLCK, and ENTRYLCK registers are fully commented out as 'not implemented', meaning hardware provides zero lock enforcement. When secure monitor software writes to register offsets 0x0040 (MDLCK), 0x0044 (MDLCKH), 0x0048 (MDCFGLCK), or 0x004C (ENTRYLCK), the register access falls through MuxLookup default (0.U) in RegMap (line 854), returning zero without latching any lock state. The cascade requirement clarified by this PR — 'if MDCFG(m) is locked, all MDCFG(0) through MDCFG(m-1) must also be locked' — cannot be enforced because MDCFGLCK.f does not exist in hardware. Consequently, MDCFG(m-1).t remains freely writable even when MDCFG(m) is supposedly locked, allowing an attacker to expand or contract the entry window of MD(m) by manipulating the preceding MDCFG entry's t field, thereby redirecting IOPMP traffic checks to unintended memory ranges.
security_spec.summary: MDLCK/MDCFGLCK/ENTRYLCK lock registers unimplemented in Chisel RTL; compromised secure monitor can arbitrarily modify IOPMP MDCFG entry boundaries to redirect DMA access checks, enabling hardware-level privilege escape
